CFTC Submits Crypto Market Rule Proposal for White House Review as CLARITY Act Stalls

A regulatory filing on the White House Office of Management and Budget (OMB) website indicates that the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) submitted a proposal to regulate cryptocurrency trading and markets on September 17. The submission follows the Senate’s failure to advance the CLARITY Act, which would have granted the CFTC primary authority over digital asset markets. The proposal is under review and has not been finalized. — link

CoinShares: Bitcoin Unlikely to Break $80K Without Inflation or Fed Shift

CoinShares said Bitcoin faces two major near-term headwinds: a more hawkish Federal Reserve and the setback to the CLARITY Act. The firm said a decisive break above $80,000 is unlikely before year-end without a meaningful improvement in inflation or a significant shift in monetary-policy expectations. It added that Bitcoin is relatively insulated from the regulatory setback, while Ethereum and other altcoins are more exposed. CoinShares also said a revised CLARITY Act could return as early as next year. — link

NYSE Plans to Enable 24/7 Onchain Trading Through Its In-Development ATS

NYSE is exploring 24/7 onchain trading through an alternative trading system (ATS) currently under development. Michael Blaugrund of Intercontinental Exchange and NYSE said Avalanche meets many of the platform’s requirements and that the teams are working closely. — link

MetaMask Launches Added Protection to Guard Against Red Pill Attacks

MetaMask has launched Added Protection, a security feature that requires the actual outcome of an Ethereum or EVM transaction to match its preview. If the result differs, the transaction automatically fails and users only lose the attempted gas fee. The feature is enabled by default on extension version 13.45 across 13 EVM networks supporting EIP-7702 smart accounts. — link

Coinbase and Stablecore Partner to Bring Digital Asset Services to 3,000+ U.S. Banks and Credit Unions

Coinbase and Stablecore are partnering to help community and regional banks and credit unions offer digital asset custody, trading and stablecoin payments through their existing banking platforms. Stablecore’s white-label infrastructure is integrated with core banking, digital banking and compliance systems serving more than 3,000 U.S. institutions, while Coinbase provides the underlying regulated digital asset infrastructure. — link
